# Symptoms and involuntary speech
Your character may automatically speak about how they feel instead of receiving a private bodily symptom message. These are ordinary local speech messages: nearby players can hear the words and see your speech bubble.
## One line every two minutes
[bold]All effects share one two-minute cooldown per character.[/bold] Being drunk, high and low on blood at the same time still produces at most one automatic symptom line every two minutes. This is a maximum frequency, not a guarantee of a line when the timer ends; an active symptom must trigger it.
## Blood loss
Low blood can make your character say "I feel faint...", "I feel dizzy...", "I need a lie down..." or a similar first-person line.
## Alcohol
Drunken characters may say "Hic...", "woo...", "Whoops..." or "heh... fuzzy...". Dizziness from blood loss or an old injury alone does not count as drunkenness for these lines.
## Chems
Drug highs from Jet, Med-X and other chems can produce remarks such as "pretty colors...", "I'm just so happy..." or "The sky is so purple...". Other medicines use more neutral remarks about feeling their effects.
## Other symptoms
Nausea, pain, hunger, thirst, radiation sickness, withdrawal and other supported bodily warnings use short, natural first-person lines. Your character speaks as "I" or "my", rather than reading a "You feel..." notification out loud.
## Who can hear it?
Speech uses your normal voice, language, local hearing range and speech effects. It is not automatically transmitted over a radio. Normal speech restrictions still apply: muted, gagged or incapacitated characters cannot bypass them. Their original private notification remains available when speech is impossible.
Speaking does not treat the cause. Blood loss, drug effects and other symptoms still need their usual care.
